species: human; human kidney/heart tissue; mammalian comparator
cell_type_model: HMC/mesangial cells stably expressing cloned human (pro)renin receptor; human kidney and heart sections
assay_or_perturbation: Renin or prorenin binding and cross-linking; receptor phosphorylation; angiotensinogen-to-angiotensin-I kinetics; ERK1/2 phosphorylation and MAPK assay
relation_type: Renin directly binds ATP6AP2/(pro)renin receptor and activates a receptor-associated ERK1/2 relay while also increasing membrane-associated angiotensin-I generation
pathway_branch: REN1-ATP6AP2 -> receptor phosphorylation and membrane renin activity -> ERK1/2/MAPK and local angiotensin-I production
limitations: The source is an expression-cloning and transfected-cell study; prorenin binding is established but its signaling potency and the contribution of angiotensin-II receptors vary by tissue. ATP6AP2 also has V-ATPase/WNT functions that were not assigned to this exact renin edge.

cell_type_model: human monocytes/THP-1 cells and humanized-resistin mice; BNL CL.2 mouse liver cells as comparator
assay_or_perturbation: Resistin-Fc affinity capture and direct binding; CAP1 overexpression or suppression; intracellular cAMP and PKA assays; inflammatory-gene transcription and in-vivo human-resistin perturbation
relation_type: Human resistin directly engages CAP1 and requires CAP1 for a cAMP/PKA inflammatory relay
pathway_branch: RETN-CAP1 -> adenylyl-cyclase/cAMP-PKA -> NF-kB-related inflammatory cytokine transcription and adipose inflammation
limitations: CAP1 is primarily a cytosolic/membrane-associated protein rather than a canonical transmembrane receptor, so the route by which extracellular resistin reaches CAP1 remains context dependent. Human and murine resistin biology is not interchangeable, and TLR4 is a separate proposed resistin receptor.

cell_type_model: Developing Xenopus forebrain; mouse cortical neurons and growth cones; mouse chondrocytes; C2C12 myoblasts
assay_or_perturbation: RGMa/NEO1 binding and loss-of-function; growth-cone-collapse and axon-guidance assays; Unc5B/LARG/FAK perturbation; BMP2-induced Smad and chondrogenesis assays; RGMa stimulation
relation_type: RGMa directly binds neogenin and can organize NEO1-associated RhoA/LARG/FAK repulsion or BMP-receptor-complex signaling
pathway_branch: RGMA-NEO1 -> Unc5B/LARG-FAK-RhoA or NEO1/BMP-receptor complex -> growth-cone collapse, axon guidance, Smad1/5/8 and chondrogenic outputs
limitations: NEO1 signaling is strongly co-receptor and context dependent; BMP2/Smad evidence is a ternary RGM-NEO1-BMP receptor context, not a claim that RGMa is the BMP ligand. Growth-cone and muscle outputs do not define one universal intracellular branch.

cell_type_model: Recombinant human RGMB/NEO1 ectodomain systems; developing mouse olfactory epithelium; structural NEO1-RGMB complex
assay_or_perturbation: Crystal structure and biophysical complex analysis; RGMB or NEO1 perturbation in olfactory epithelial differentiation; receptor-complex and developmental readouts
relation_type: RGMB directly forms a signaling-competent NEO1 dimer/complex and is required for context-specific differentiation, but an isolated RGMB-specific cytosolic relay is not resolved
pathway_branch: RGMB-NEO1 -> NEO1 dimerization/complex assembly -> olfactory epithelial differentiation and other context-specific RGM outputs
limitations: The strongest exact molecular evidence is structural and the functional study is tissue specific; the NEO1 juxtamembrane arrangement is not a direct measurement of a unique downstream kinase/adaptor. BMP/GDF ternary complexes and RGMA guidance phenotypes were not collapsed into an RGMB-specific relay.

species: human; rat/mouse comparator; recombinant receptor systems

assay_or_perturbation: Relaxin binding/agonism; receptor-domain and autoinhibition perturbations; cAMP, PKA, p38 and CREB phosphorylation; PPARgamma reporter and dominant-negative CREB assays

pathway_branch: RLN1-RXFP1 -> Gs/Gi/o and signalosome -> cAMP-PKA-p38/CREB -> PPARgamma/PGC1alpha and tissue-specific relaxin functions
limitations: RXFP1 signaling is ligand concentration, receptor conformation and cell-context dependent, with multiple G-protein branches. CREB was measured in a relaxin/RXFP1 PPARgamma assay but is a provisional endpoint, not a direct receptor-TF interaction.

species: human recombinant receptor systems; rat/mouse comparator
cell_type_model: HEK293/CHO cells expressing human RXFP1; recombinant relaxin-family receptor and peptide systems

species: human; rat; mouse comparator; recombinant receptor systems
cell_type_model: HEK293/CHO cells expressing RXFP3; recombinant relaxin-3 and receptor mutants; rat brain RXFP3 systems

pathway_branch: RLN3-RXFP3 -> Gi/o -> inhibition of cAMP and ERK1/2/MAPK -> context-specific neuroendocrine and behavioral outputs
limitations: RXFP3 signaling is ligand biased and heterologous-cell coupling does not establish one universal neuronal endpoint. Binding/activation studies include human recombinant receptors and rodent comparators; no terminal TF was directly established.

species: human recombinant receptor systems; mammalian comparator

pathway_branch: RLN3-RXFP4 -> relaxin-family GPCR coupling -> cAMP/G-protein signaling; downstream branch is receptor- and assay-dependent
limitations: The exact structural and activation evidence is strongest in recombinant human RXFP4; RXFP4 physiology and coupling differ across species, and RXFP3 remains the native RLN3 receptor in brain. No terminal TF endpoint was established.

species: human; mouse comparator; recombinant protein systems

pathway_branch: RPS19 dimer-C5AR1 -> Gi protein and Ca2+/PI3K/PLC -> ERK or p38 MAPK -> monocyte chemotaxis and leukocyte inflammatory outputs

cell_type_model: HEK293/HEK293T cells expressing LGR5; mouse intestinal crypts and organoids; recombinant LGR5/WNT receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: RSPO1-LGR5 binding; LGR5 loss/rescue and co-immunoprecipitation; WNT3A+RSPO1 TOPFLASH or beta-catenin reporter; LRP6 phosphorylation; LGR5-LRP6-FZD internalization studies
relation_type: RSPO1 directly engages LGR5 and enhances WNT receptor-complex signaling through an LGR5/FZD-LRP6 module

limitations: LGR5 is a facultative WNT receptor-complex component and its endocytosis can be dispensable for signaling; exact ternary stoichiometry and the contribution of LGR5 versus LGR4 are context dependent. TCF/LEF is a reporter endpoint, not a direct LGR5-TF edge.

cell_type_model: HEK293 RSPO/WNT receptor systems with LGR4/5/6 re-expression; mouse intestinal crypt and stem-cell contexts
assay_or_perturbation: LGR6 re-expression rescue of RSPO1 enhancement after LGR4 loss; R-spondin-LGR binding panel; WNT3A/RSPO reporter and WNT-receptor association

limitations: The exact LGR6 evidence is strongest as binding-panel and receptor-specific rescue rather than a purified RSPO1-LGR6 structure; most mechanistic work emphasizes LGR4/5. LGR6-specific endogenous tissue outputs and complex stoichiometry remain unresolved.

species: human; mouse comparator; recombinant protein systems
cell_type_model: HEK293/HEK293T cells expressing LRP6; purified LRP6 ectodomain and recombinant RSPO1; WNT reporter systems

relation_type: RSPO1 directly binds the LRP6 ectodomain in biochemical assays and potentiates LRP6-dependent WNT signaling
pathway_branch: RSPO1-LRP6 -> LRP6 phosphorylation/receptor-complex stabilization -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF signaling
limitations: Direct LRP6 binding was reported in purified/overexpression assays but was difficult to detect in some intact-cell assays and can be influenced by heparan-sulfate proteoglycans and LGR context. This row does not imply that LRP6 is the sole RSPO1 receptor.

cell_type_model: Recombinant RNF43 ectodomain and RSPO Furin domains; HEK293/HEK293T WNT receptor systems; intestinal stem-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: RNF43-RSPO complex/co-immunoprecipitation and RSPO-domain mutagenesis; RNF43/ZNRF3 perturbation; WNT receptor turnover and beta-catenin reporter assays

pathway_branch: RSPO1-RNF43 -> LGR-RSPO-E3-ligase complex -> reduced FZD/LRP ubiquitination and increased beta-catenin/TCF-LEF WNT signaling
limitations: RNF43 is a transmembrane E3 ligase and pathway brake rather than a classical kinase receptor; the exact LGR, FZD and LRP composition varies. The WNT/TCF output is a complex-level endpoint, not a direct RNF43-TF interaction.

cell_type_model: Recombinant ZNRF3 ectodomain with RSPO1 or RSPO2 Furin domains; LGR5-RSPO1-ZNRF3 structural and biophysical systems; WNT reporter and receptor-turnover models
assay_or_perturbation: Crystal structure, binding/competition and RSPO-domain perturbation; ZNRF3/RNF43 loss-of-function; Frizzled ubiquitination and WNT reporter assays
relation_type: RSPO1 directly binds ZNRF3 and blocks its WNT-receptor ubiquitin-ligase activity in an LGR-RSPO receptor complex
pathway_branch: RSPO1-ZNRF3 -> LGR-RSPO-E3-ligase complex -> preserved FZD/LRP surface receptors -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF signaling
limitations: The structural study resolves the ZNRF3 ectodomain/RSPO1 interface but the signaling complex also includes LGR and WNT receptors; ZNRF3 neutralization is not a direct intracellular kinase relay and stoichiometry is context dependent.

pathway_branch: RSPO2-LGR4 -> LGR/RNF43-ZNRF3 and FZD-LRP WNT signalosome -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF pathway and developmental outputs
limitations: RSPO2 has unusually strong LGR-independent activity in some systems; the exact contribution of LGR4 versus HSPGs and ZNRF3/RNF43 varies by tissue. TOPFLASH/WNT reporters are pathway endpoints rather than direct LGR4-TF measurements.

cell_type_model: HEK293/HEK293T cells expressing LGR5; recombinant R-spondin/LGR systems; intestinal and WNT reporter models
assay_or_perturbation: RSPO2-LGR5 binding and WNT reporter assays; LGR5 receptor-complex association; ZNRF3/RNF43 and WNT-receptor perturbations

pathway_branch: RSPO2-LGR5 -> LGR5/RNF43-ZNRF3 and FZD-LRP complex -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF WNT potentiation
limitations: The direct LGR5 binding and downstream WNT evidence are strongest in heterologous systems; RSPO2 can also signal through HSPGs without LGRs, so this exact pair is not the sole route to the phenotype.

cell_type_model: Recombinant human/mouse RSPO2 Furin domains and RNF43 ectodomain; HAP1 WNT reporter cells; developmental models

pathway_branch: RSPO2-RNF43 -> E3-ligase neutralization and FZD/LRP receptor preservation -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF WNT signaling
limitations: The structural and functional mechanisms differ by species and cell context, and RSPO2 can use HSPG-mediated LGR-independent signaling. RNF43 neutralization is a receptor-complex/pathway edge, not a direct intracellular kinase-to-TF interaction.

cell_type_model: Recombinant ZNRF3 ectodomain and RSPO2 Furin domains; HAP1 WNT reporter and developmental models
assay_or_perturbation: RSPO2-ZNRF3 crystal/biophysical complex; domain-mutant loss of signaling; ZNRF3 perturbation and WNT receptor-turnover assays
relation_type: RSPO2 directly binds and inhibits ZNRF3, preserving WNT receptor availability in a receptor-complex relay
pathway_branch: RSPO2-ZNRF3 -> E3-ligase inhibition and FZD/LRP receptor preservation -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF WNT signaling
limitations: ZNRF3 is a membrane E3-ligase pathway regulator and RSPO2 signaling can be LGR-independent through HSPGs; receptor complex composition and developmental direction are context dependent. No direct ZNRF3-TF interaction is inferred.

assay_or_perturbation: RSPO3-LGR4 binding and Kd measurements; LGR4 knockdown/rescue; TOPFLASH and WNT3A/RSPO3 reporter assays; LRP6 dependence; endogenous RSPO3-LGR4 perturbation

pathway_branch: RSPO3-LGR4 -> LGR4/RNF43-ZNRF3 and LRP6/FZD signalosome -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF WNT and tissue-specific outputs
limitations: RSPO3 can potentiate WNT without LGRs through HSPGs, and it also has an SDC4-dependent PCP branch. The exact LGR4 contribution varies by model; reporter output is not a direct LGR4-TF interaction.

pathway_branch: RSPO3-LGR5 -> LGR5/RNF43-ZNRF3 and FZD-LRP receptor availability -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF and gastric/intestinal stem-cell outputs
limitations: The exact receptor binding and reporter data are strongest in engineered systems, while tissue studies add context-specific Lgr5-positive outputs. RSPO3 also has LGR-independent and SDC4/HSPG-associated branches that were kept separate.

species: human; Xenopus comparator; mammalian cell systems
